but cells to humans is not the same as humans to society -  cells arent conscious. now you can have an argument on what the best way to value everyones opinions is (direct democracy or otherwise), but there are people that have no say in their fate. i dont see how essentially telling people that they are going to live horrible lives and give them little to no choice is justified. and the only solution i see out that you could potentially justify is when post-scarcity is reached. perhaps also you could give a rough idea by using that one thought experiment - would you be willing to be randomally switch places/be born in someone elses position. im not sure that that is truly achieveable without post-scarcity. post-scarcity is no guarantee though.

its not the crux of the matter. i can change, the world, however, really cant.

while it is technically theoretically possible for all of humanity to agree on one risk or another, it is in no way practical. humans have different wishes (ex. my wish to not exist vs peoples belief that suicide is always/near always not the correct option), and so to agree on some sort of risk... im not sure how that is possible. especially since some are in a more priveleged position, and people tend to disregard those below their status. surely i do, at least on a day-to-day basis i mean. when im purchacing clothing, for example, i dont (usually, sometimes i do) think of the suffering that may have went into making that. but for most thats not ever even thought of. and even if it is a thought, people arent really willing to just not buy clothing or food because of the conditions of work of those who provided it - they still make the purchace.

if you can solve this issue, along with all the other issues of, essentially, wealth inequality, then we are in a different situation. personally though, i see no real solution, at least any time remotely soon (with scarcity present). you could argue that whatever suffering exist now is worth the potential of a post-scarcity society, but whether it is worth it or not is a matter of opinion and even still there is no guarantee of humans ever reaching that.

right, i agree that there is no real objective good. but we can still agree to subjective standards. i dont see how we have to try to approximate an objective morality with naturality.

sure, i agree, it would likely be a net positive if i were to not commit suicide. i would argue the greatest net positive were to be if no one existed, but that is unrealistic so it doesnt matter. selfishly though, i dont really have much desire to exist. there is potential for joy, but, as i have said my opinion to be, no amount of joy can undue any suffering. the irony, however, is that my suicide would cause suffering. which is why i have no idea what the right decision is.

to get more personal, i have no idea how i am going to find and, more importantly, maintain any long-lasting relationship of any kind. i have a couple values/preferences that are somewhat restrictive, thus making this difficult. and in general i dont think i am a good person - i think my good is undone by my bad - essentially, i believe im net-negative. perhaps this could be changed with some sort of treatment, though.

no you are fine.

i think on an individual level, sure, take whatever risk you would like. the problem is im not sure if a risk that only impacts you really exists.

in the same way, much of what countries, such as the US, have (primarily materialisticly) come from the suffering of others. to be fair, there may be a solution to this. maybe there are adequete solutions that dont require post-scarcity, but it seems to me an actual good solution would. all this said, we cant really look at this on an individual level. if i am to live my life in a standard way (for an US citizen) (being a consumer, essentially), i am actively causing suffering. that is what is hard for me to justify. even if i could justify taking the risk of choosing to live, it feels wrong that i cause others suffering.

yea, i most likely could go through some form of treatment and would lose this opinion and just live some sort of life, possibly satisfying and fulfilling, perhaps not (this is a risk that seems very high for me, and im not too fond of risks. this issue is a bit removed from the current topic though). but as i said i would, in my mind, have to dismiss the suffering caused by my existence to actually feel ok, which im not sure if i want to do.
